clue.text: Extremely hairy Philistine reaches party in high spirits

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here of both hairy and Philistine

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

explanation.surface: A very hairy uncultured man arrives at a party already buzzing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' applies to both 'hairy' and 'Philistine', giving HY and PE. The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone excited and overstimulated is said to be wound up or buzzing, an idiom for high spirits.

clue.text: "Hello, sailor" is appropriate, when moving

parts.note: hi is a greeting
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is greeted, and someone points out that's fitting given the motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective but is a verb: to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize a vehicle in transit, such as a plane or lorry, is to commandeer it.

clue.text: Devout former judge and governor

parts.note: PI, short for pious, means devout
late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: A pious ex-judge who once ran a province.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is crossword shorthand for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontius Pilate was the Roman prefect of Judaea who presided at the trial of Jesus.

clue.text: Copies potential partners, keeping mostly upbeat?

indicators.note: the dates keep, hold, the other letters inside them

parts.note: dates are people one goes out with, possible partners

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: read as up plus beat, and to lick is to beat

explanation.surface: Copies of possible partners who stay cheerful, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upbeat' looks like 'cheerful' but splits as UP + LICK (beat); 'mostly' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact reproductions of something are copies of it, the plural noun.

clue.text: President leading a merry dance?

indicators.note: the president comes before, leading, the a

parts.note: James K. Polk was the eleventh US president

explanation.surface: A head of state leads everyone a merry dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a merry dance' suggests a runaround, but this is a lively Bohemian dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively Bohemian couple dance in duple time is a cheerful one.

clue.text: In 26 without, say, a type of hat

definitions.meaning: the answer to 26 across, a feudal subject, minus EG (say, for example) leaves a fib, and this phrase is rhyming slang for one
a flat-crowned felt hat with a turned-up brim

explanation.surface: A puzzle reference wrapped round a description of headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 across is LIEGE; without EG ('say') it is LIE. Cockney rhyming slang uses this phrase (often shortened to 'porky') for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang turns a fib into this savoury snack's name, and the same name belongs to a flat-crowned hat.

clue.text: "Biopic strewn with lust, not love" (Advertiser)

indicators.note: things strewn are scattered about, so the letters of biopic and lust are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A film review: a life story littered with desire but no romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strewn' rearranges the two words; 'not love' takes an O (love is zero in tennis) out of the pool first.
explanation.definitionFit: A press agent promotes clients and products, so is one who advertises.

clue.text: Thin artist reluctantly eating starters

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist

indicators.note: starters are first courses, so the first letters of reluctantly and eating

explanation.surface: A skinny painter only picks at the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin' looks like the artist's build but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare in the sense of sparse or tenuous, as in rare mountain air, means thin.

clue.text: Hook holding one black French dressing gown

indicators.note: the hook holds the one inside it

parts.note: a peg is a hook to hang things on
I is the Roman numeral one
noir is French for black

explanation.surface: A hanger bearing a single black French dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black French' is one piece: the French word for black.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's light loose robe worn over a nightdress is a negligee-like dressing gown.

clue.text: Spared once seduced, when short of time

parts.note: ex means former, once

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the T is dropped

parts.note: tempted means seduced, enticed

explanation.surface: A lover who was once led astray escaped when time ran out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes the first T from TEMPTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being let off a duty or a charge means being excused from it, freed.

clue.text: Frenchman with money for second drink

indicators.note: one thing put for another is substituted in its place, so money takes the place of the second

parts.note: Jules is a typical French man's name
P (penny, pence) stands for money

explanation.surface: A French man exchanges cash for another round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is S, the last letter of JULES, which is swapped for P.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint julep is a sweet bourbon cocktail, so the word names a drink.

clue.text: Rake one chap used in occupation

indicators.note: pieces used in something are put inside it, so the chap and the one go into the occupation

parts.note: one's line is one's line of work, an occupation
Bert is a stock man's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A garden rake that one man uses for his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like a garden tool but is a dissolute man.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeker, which is exactly what this word for a debauchee means.

clue.text: Some lemon has HNO3 containing carbon instead of nitrogen

indicators.note: the formula is to contain a different element, so it signals that something new goes in
carbon comes instead of nitrogen, so one element's symbol takes the other's place in the formula's name

parts.note: HNO3 is the chemical formula of nitric acid
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on what is in lemon juice compared with nitric acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nitrogen' names the N swapped out of NITRIC; the clue word carbon is used once, so its leaf sits inside the indicator phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemons are rich in this acid, which gives citrus fruit its sour taste.

clue.text: Party without a break

indicators.note: in the old sense outside, so the party goes round the a

parts.note: the SNP is the Scottish National Party

explanation.surface: A political party that never takes a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to break suddenly and cleanly, as a twig does.

clue.text: City about right latitude for common sort of golf tournament

indicators.note: the city goes about, round, the right

parts.note: Stoke-on-Trent is an English city
play means latitude, freedom of movement

explanation.surface: A city's position used for an ordinary golf event.
explanation.walkthrough: STOKE (Stoke-on-Trent, a city in England's Midlands) goes round R. 'latitude' suggests geography but means room to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Most professional golf events are scored by total shots taken, rather than holes won.

clue.text: Puzzling row about a cowshed (hint: suspect not English)

indicators.note: the row goes about, round, everything else in the clue

parts.note: a line is a row

indicators.note: not English means the E is left out of the cowshed word

parts.note: a byre is a cowshed

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dodgy, so the letters of hint are shuffled

explanation.surface: A dispute over a farm building, with a tip that it is not English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges the hint word; 'not English' takes the E out of the byre (cowshed). 'about' puts the whole lot inside the row.
explanation.definitionFit: Something maze-like is so intricate it is hard to work out, so it is bewildering.

clue.text: Standard measures for ale? That's right

parts.note: a yard of ale is a tall glass, a measure of beer
a tick marks something as right

explanation.surface: Pub talk about how much beer makes a standard serving.
explanation.walkthrough: A yard of ale is a traditional English tall glass holding about two and a half pints.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark used to judge things against is a standard of comparison.

clue.text: Stops only child Penny filling in part of crossword

parts.note: o.c. is the abbreviation for only child

indicators.note: the penny fills, goes inside, the part of crossword

parts.note: clues are part of a crossword
D, from Latin denarius, is an old penny

explanation.surface: A lone child blocks a coin from going into the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: D was the abbreviation for the old British penny, before decimal currency in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: To block or close an opening or passage is to obstruct it, so stops.

clue.text: Stop for a time in Bury, meeting male having sex

parts.note: to inter is to bury
it is a slang word for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: In the Lancashire town of Bury, a man is caught having sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the town in Lancashire but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend or pause briefly and then resume is to interrupt something temporarily.

clue.text: Making holy doctors snort cocaine

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of snort and cocaine are rearranged

explanation.surface: Medics caught taking drugs, oddly linked with sanctity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctors' looks like medics but is a verb: SNORT COCAINE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Dedicating something to God in a formal rite sanctifies it.

clue.text: Topless match, with players from one side in shades

indicators.note: without its top, the first letter is removed

parts.note: to agree is to match
in bridge North and South are partners, one side

explanation.surface: A topless game with one team wearing sunglasses.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as partners against East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Hues of the colour of grass are greens, so these are shades of colour.

clue.text: Blind test?

definitions.meaning: a blind is a ..., a window cover
to ... is to test, as in medical ...

explanation.surface: An experiment done without seeing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a blind trial, but the two words are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A window cover that blocks view is a blind, and checking people for disease is testing.

clue.text: Broadcast fictions which give substance to soaps?

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the word for fictions is given by its pronunciation

parts.note: lies are fictions, untruths

explanation.surface: Untrue storylines on air that make TV soap operas what they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soaps' suggests TV soap operas, whose plots are fictions; in fact soap is made with alkali solutions.
explanation.definitionFit: These alkaline solutions are used in making soap, giving it its substance.

clue.text: My crime? Sat around, being crooked

indicators.note: letters sent around are moved about, so my crime sat is rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer confesses to idling about while being dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' looks like 'dishonest' but means lopsided.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lopsided lacks balance between its two sides, so it is unsymmetrical.

clue.text: In power, May's tense

definitions.meaning: the past tense of the verb may

explanation.surface: Theresa May is nervous while in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' suggests Theresa May, the former Prime Minister, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength or force, and also the past form of the modal verb may.

clue.text: Old man, twice party leader

definitions.note: the leader of party is its first letter, P, spoken thus in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: twice means the old man's letters appear two times in a row

parts.note: pa is a father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A veteran who has twice led a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet P, the first letter of party, is said this way.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio spelling alphabet's code word for the letter P stands for party's initial.

clue.text: Journo backed definition that's undignified

indicators.note: backed here means turned back to front, so the journalist's letters are read the other way

parts.note: ED, an editor, is a journalist
a definition gives a word's meaning

explanation.surface: A reporter supported a definition that was beneath them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like 'supported' but turns ED into DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that lowers one's standing or self-respect is degrading, the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Subject of story told by Georgia

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib
GE is the abbreviation for Georgia

explanation.surface: The topic of a tale someone from Georgia told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' looks like a topic but is a feudal vassal.
explanation.definitionFit: A vassal owing feudal service is a subject of the lord he serves.

clue.text: Problem getting old Times supplement?

parts.note: TES stood for the Times Educational Supplement; written the other way round those letters spell set

explanation.surface: Difficulty getting hold of a back issue of a newspaper supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as SET BACK, which gives TES. 'old' because the TES is no longer an actual supplement to The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse or hitch that halts progress is a difficulty, a problem.

clue.text: Go wrong injecting soft enzyme

indicators.note: the go and the wrong take in the soft as if injected

parts.note: a go is a try
a sin is a wrong
P (piano) means soft in music

explanation.surface: A failed attempt at injecting a mild enzyme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go wrong' reads as 'fail' but is two pieces, TRY and SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This digestive protein made by the pancreas breaks down proteins in the gut.
